title: Pinchas ben Guvta of Ariach
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: An incident concerning him is cited in [Sifrei Bamidbar, Balak 131:2](https://www.sefaria.org/Sifrei_Bamidbar.131.2). He was rolling barrels when the spirit of Peor came to him. He brandished the spit against the spirit, which fled and went away. The spirit returned to him a second time at night and asked: “Why are you cursing me?” He replied: “I will not curse you again from now on.”[^1] In the [Jerusalem Talmud, Sanhedrin, chapter Chelek, halakhah 2](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Sanhedrin.10.2.16), the name reads “Menahem of Gufta-Ariach.”[^2]

notes.text: Hyman calls the source ‘Sifra, Balak’; the corresponding story is in Sifrei Bamidbar 131:2. Penei Moshe explains that the spirit came to provoke the man for cursing it. Guggenheimer describes the Yerushalmi version as fragmentary.
Hyman reports the Yerushalmi name as מנחם איש נופתה אריה; Guggenheimer reads מנחם איש גופתה אריח, ‘Menahem of Gufta-Ariach.’
